entry.evidence: However, only a few studies have combined apparent groundwater ages, or the raw tracer concentrations, with 3D numerical models

steps.action: Set the objectives: characterize the Neogene aquifer's flow systems with tracer ages, hydrochemistry and stable isotopes, and check the existing conceptual flow model against particle-tracking ages.
steps.quote: The main objectives of this contribution are to: i) characterize groundwater flow systems using apparent tracer ages

steps.action: Took as a starting point the earlier 14C model ages (0.6-6.5 kyr) of Coetsiers and Walraevens (2009), whose co-author Walraevens is an author here, and noted that the deep aquifer had not been sampled.
steps.quote: However, these ages might not be representative for the whole aquifer as the deepest areas of the aquifer were not sampled.

steps.action: Sampled 22 piezometers at 8 locations in March 2019 and analysed stable water isotopes, 3H-3He, 4He, Ne, δ13C, 14C and major and minor ions, with noble gases taken in duplicate copper tubes.
steps.quote: A total of 22 piezometers at 8 selected locations were sampled across the Nete catchment within the Neogene aquifer

steps.action: Compiled hydrochemical and isotopic data from earlier campaigns (Van Keer et al. 1999; Coetsiers and Walraevens 2006, 2009; cAt 2005; Rogiers et al. unpublished 2016) with the new data.
steps.quote: from which their collected data have been compiled in this work.

steps.action: Checked analytical quality by ionic balance error against a 5 % threshold, and accepted errors up to 11 % for weakly mineralized waters.
steps.quote: The quality of the analytical results of the measured ions was evaluated by determining their ionic balance errors (threshold < 5 %).

steps.action: Used the steady-state MODFLOW-2005 flow model of the catchment, built and calibrated with particle swarm optimization in the authors' earlier work, as the basis for advective transport.
steps.quote: A MODFLOW-2005 (Harbaugh et al., 2005) steady-state groundwater flow model has been developed for the Nete catchment

steps.action: Compared the new hydrochemistry and Stuyfzand water types with the published regional characterization and found them consistent.
steps.quote: The obtained results are in accordance with the published results of Coetsiers and Walraevens (2006) for regional characterization of the Neogene aquifer.

steps.action: Inferred the processes along the flow path (pyrite oxidation, cation exchange of the freshening type, dilution of connate NaCl water below the Boom Clay) from the Piper and Na/Cl-Cl diagrams.
steps.quote: Similarly to Walraevens (1990), the groundwater quality evolution as a result from freshening is shown in Fig. 4.

steps.action: Built a local meteoric water line from GNIP data and compared the groundwater δ2H-δ18O with it, inferring modern meteoric recharge and, for depleted deep samples, older and colder-climate water.
steps.quote: The clustering of a large number of groundwater samples around the LMWL indicates that local modern meteoric water is a significant source of groundwater recharge

steps.action: Compared the new δ13C and 14C data and their evolution along the flow direction with Coetsiers and Walraevens (2009) and found them closely consistent.
steps.quote: The results obtained from the laboratory analysis performed on the samples in the current campaign closely follow the results presented by Coetsiers and Walraevens (2009)

steps.action: Applied the Coetsiers and Walraevens (2009) mass-balance correction model, which partitions DIC among recharge CO2, calcite, Fe and SO4 reduction and methanogenesis, to estimate initial 14C activities.
steps.quote: a correction model is applied to the 14C initial activities

steps.action: Reproduced the published Coetsiers and Walraevens (2009) results to validate the workflow, then checked calculated against measured δ13C.
steps.quote: For the sake of quality control, we first reproduced the results obtained by Coetsiers and Walraevens (2009) to validate our workflow

steps.action: Assuming fossil organic matter gave negative model ages, so they revised the auxiliary assumption to recent dissolved organic matter carrying 100 pMC.
steps.quote: Negative model ages were obtained if CRecharge was left as the only C source

steps.action: Obtained corrected 14C ages, mostly 1-10 kyr, rising to 15-33 kyr in the deepest Berchem & Voort and Eigenbilzen filters, and read them as upper limits.
steps.quote: the corrected 14C model ages for samples R-2c, R-34c and R-54c resulted in larger age estimates, from 15 to 33 kyr.

steps.action: Computed Pearson (1965) corrected ages for comparison and found them older than the chosen model's, most at low 14C activity.
steps.quote: The Pearson (1965) model largely overestimates the age when the measured 14C activity is low in relation to the Coetsiers and Walraevens (2009) model

steps.action: Estimated 3H/3He apparent ages: shallow filters are modern (years to tens of years), several tritium-poor filters exceed 66 years, R-6a and R-6b have unexplained high tritium, and young deep wells near the Rauw Fault are attributed to converging flowlines.
steps.quote: Thus, they characterize the youngest groundwater component measured in the aquifer.

steps.action: Plotted 3H/3He ages against corrected 14C ages to identify samples that mix tritium-bearing and tritium-free water, and linked them to water subtypes and formations.
steps.quote: This serves as an indication of the zones where water mixing with a stronger dominance of older components takes place in the Neogene aquifer

steps.action: Checked the plausibility of the 3H/3He and 14C ages against radiogenic 4He accumulation and against 3He/4He versus Ne/He, separating radiogenic old water from tritiogenic young water.
steps.quote: The plausibility of the calculated 3H/3He and 14C model ages can be evaluated

steps.action: Ran MODPATH 7 backward particle tracking (10 × 10 × 10 particles per screened cell) on the flow model to compute advective age distributions at each well.
steps.quote: to check whether the estimated model ages from age tracers are consistent with the modelled groundwater flow velocities.

steps.action: Compared the advective age distributions with the tracer ages: agreement for young (≤100 yr) and old (>1 kyr) water, the strongest discrepancies at 100-1000 yr.
steps.quote: Groundwater with groundwater flow model advective ages of ~ 100 yr or younger (i.e. R-6a to R-51a) show a good agreement

steps.action: Attributed the mismatch at intermediate ages to the model's neglect of dispersion and to tracer limitations, not to the flow model or the conceptual model.
steps.quote: The advective age distribution at each filter is relatively narrow and unimodal as a consequence of not accounting for mixing by dispersion.

steps.action: Kept the Coetsiers and Walraevens (2009) correction model as adequate, because the old 14C ages match the particle-tracking ages in order of magnitude.
steps.quote: This confirms that the reactions and processes influencing the total C in the aquifer considered in the correction model

steps.action: Combined tracers, isotopes, hydrochemistry and model ages into a refined conceptual cross-section of local, intermediate (mixed) and semi-regional flow systems, including flow along the Rauw Fault.
steps.quote: Fig. 11 shows an interpretation of the flow paths carrying groundwater with different ages (young and old, and their mixture)

steps.action: Kept the hypothesis of shallow local and deep semi-regional flow systems, with a mixed zone in the centre of the aquifer.
steps.quote: allowed us to validate the hypothesis regarding the distribution of groundwater flow systems

steps.action: Posed the next question: close the 100-1000 yr age gap with 39Ar and 4He model ages, and quantify the sources of radiogenic 4He.
steps.quote: additional tracers (e.g.39Ar, with a half-life of 269 years) may be useful to close the age gap

tree.answer: Partly: wells at many depths and locations stand in for repetitions along flow paths
Agreement across tracers and model for young and old water; discrepancy at 100-1000 yr absorbed by auxiliaries
Three flow systems with a central mixing zone kept as the joint interpretation

end.claim: The Neogene aquifer holds three flow systems: a shallow local system of modern meteoric water, a deep semi-regional system of old water with significant radiogenic 4He, and a central mixed zone where young recharge mixes with discharging old water.

decisive_move.sentence: The 2019 campaign, which sampled 3H/3He, 4He, Ne, 14C, stable isotopes and hydrochemistry at the same filters, including the previously unsampled deep aquifer, produced the coexistence of young and old tracers on which the mixing claim rests.

gates.evidence: Sampling aimed at completeness, not at a hypothesis: 'The sampling strategy was focused on getting a complete data set' (p. 4). The particle-tracking comparison could have failed and did mismatch for 100-1000 yr water; the mismatch was attributed to dispersion and tracer limits (p. 15). The flow-system hypothesis is named only at the end (p. 16-17), and nothing was fixed before the data.

imports.item: Quadrupole mass spectrometry for 4He, Ne and 3He/4He, and tritium by 3He ingrowth (HELIS Bremen)
ICP-MS and molecular spectrometry for major and minor ions
Standard Particle Swarm Optimization (spso11) used in calibrating the inherited flow model
Bomb-pulse 14C and 3H from atmospheric nuclear tests as a marker of post-1955 recharge

novelty_claims.quote: [...] the first multitracer study performed in the region.

limits: Locations: the XML text holds only the abstract and captions, so body steps are cited by printed page and their quotes come from the PDF text (superscripts flattened, e.g. 3H/3He). No review file was supplied, so there is no review sequence. The supplement (ESM-1 to ESM-4), which holds the correction-model details, the δ13C checks and the full chemistry, was not supplied; the coded checks rely on main-text statements. Data are available only on request. The flow-system 'hypothesis' appears only in the conceptual-model section and the conclusion; that it guided the work beforehand is not shown (inference). The entry also has an external_goal element: the work is funded and framed by the ONDRAF/NIRAS disposal programme (p. 1, p. 17). The flow model and its calibration are inherited from Casillas-Trasvina et al. (2021); no sensitivity of the advective ages to recharge, conductivity or dispersion is reported. Two wells were not fully purged (footnote 1, p. 5), and the high tritium in R-6a and R-6b is left unexplained (p. 10). Noble gases were sampled in duplicate, but duplicate agreement is not reported. Sub-claims and statuses: the Coetsiers and Walraevens (2009) correction model is adequate (best_explanation, order-of-magnitude agreement only, ages are upper limits); 3H/3He is usable at shallow depth (<~100 m) and in the thin western aquifer, and 14C distinguishes old water in the centre and east (capability_characterized, qualitative); 100-1000 yr waters are mixtures (best_explanation, unresolved by the current tracers); 4He-rad comes mainly from the Boom Clay and deeper sources (best_explanation, not quantified).

disagreements.target: Coetsiers and Walraevens (2009) 14C model ages for the aquifer
disagreements.support: The earlier ages lacked the deepest parts of the aquifer, which the new campaign samples, yielding ages up to 15-33 kyr.
disagreements.quote: However, these ages might not be representative for the whole aquifer as the deepest areas of the aquifer were not sampled.

disagreements.target: Classical 14C correction models compared by Van Keer et al. (1999) (Vogel, Tamers, Pearson, Mook, F&G, IAEA, Evans, Eichinger)
disagreements.support: They consider only a few reactions, while the aquifer's carbon is shaped by calcite dissolution, organic-matter oxidation, sulphate reduction and methanogenesis.
disagreements.quote: However, these models are not as robust as required for the Neogene aquifer since they only consider [...] .

disagreements.support: Side-by-side corrected ages in Table 4 show the Pearson ages older than the chosen model's, most at low 14C activity.
disagreements.quote: The Pearson (1965) model largely overestimates the age when the measured 14C activity is low in relation to the Coetsiers and Walraevens (2009) model

disagreements.target: PHYMOL 14C model ages (Van Keer et al., 1999)
disagreements.support: Insufficient chemistry data were collected to apply the full mass-balance correction, so those ages are only upper-limit indications.
disagreements.quote: the uncertainty of their calculated 14C model ages is probably substantial

disagreements.target: Previously proposed conceptual models of the study area
disagreements.support: The joint tracer and particle-tracking interpretation adds a central young/old mixing zone and flow along the Rauw Fault.
disagreements.quote: These results have helped us to refine previously proposed conceptual models for the study area

alternatives_considered.reason: The classical models consider only a few reactions; the chosen model was built for the same aquifer
